In standard LaTeX (without the `caption` package), you can control caption alignment by changing the internal macro `\@makecaption`. The simplest way is to use the `\makeatletter...\makeatother` trick in the preamble and make the caption use a `\parbox` with `\raggedright`.

Put this in your preamble:

```latex
\makeatletter
\long\def\@makecaption#1#2{%
  \vskip\abovecaptionskip
  \sbox\@tempboxa{#1: #2}%
  \ifdim \wd\@tempboxa >\hsize
    \parbox{\hsize}{\raggedright #1: #2}\par
  \else
    {\raggedright \mbox{#1: #2}\par}%
  \fi
  \vskip\belowcaptionskip}
\makeatother
```

This makes *all* figure and table captions left-aligned.

### If you want it only for tables
You can locally redefine it around a single table:

```latex
\begin{table}
\makeatletter
\long\def\@makecaption#1#2{%
  \vskip\abovecaptionskip
  \parbox{\hsize}{\raggedright #1: #2}\par
  \vskip\belowcaptionskip}
\makeatother

\caption{This table caption is left-aligned.}
\centering
\begin{tabular}{cc}
A & B\\
\end{tabular}
\end{table}
```

Notes:
- This affects the label format too (`Table 1: ...`). If you want a different separator (e.g., a period instead of `:`), change `#1: #2` accordingly.
- `\raggedright` avoids justification; if you want fully justified but not centered, that’s a different setup.

If you tell me your document class (`article`, `report`, `IEEEtran`, etc.), I can adjust the redefinition to match its default caption style while only changing alignment.
